metadata.note: BART (San Francisco Bay Area Rapid Transit District), 1972 to today, modelled as one feature per route per service pattern, with non-overlapping years per route, so the slider shows each route only over the track its trains actually ran in that era. Each year draws the pattern in effect at the end of that year: an extension appears from the year it opened (Pittsburg/Bay Point from 1996 although it opened December 7), a cutback from the year it took effect. Peak-only and evening-only extensions are drawn, and named in the segment note, because they are regular passenger service. eBART and the Oakland Airport Connector are separate features because both are physically separate systems with a forced transfer.
metadata.method: Geometry: every era is clipped from the agency GTFS shapes (feed_version 72) between its two terminal stations. The direct San Bruno - Millbrae track bypassing SFO, used 2003 and 2008-2023 but by no current trip, is real-traced from OSM railway=subway ways. No straight-line legs. Service history: the Wikipedia articles for each BART line, History of Bay Area Rapid Transit (expansion timeline and defunct lines) and the BART chronology through March 2009, cited per segment.
metadata.traced_vs_documented: Station-to-station traced lengths against BART-published segment mileages: Fremont - MacArthur 25.7 mi traced vs 28 mi documented for the 1972 opening; Richmond extension 10.3 vs 11; Concord - MacArthur 18.9 vs 17 (traced includes MacArthur - Rockridge running to the junction); Montgomery - Daly City 7.5 vs 7.5; eBART 9.2 vs 10.1; Oakland Airport Connector 3.2 vs 3.2. Documented figures include tail tracks and junction approaches, which station-clipped geometry leaves out.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) Every historical headway_min is an estimate; only the 2026 segments are counted from a timetable (GTFS), plus the 2003 Purple Line shuttle's 20 minutes. Pre-2026 frequencies, including the COVID-19 reductions of 2020-21 and the 20-minute base schedule of the 2020s, were not checked. (2) Colma, 1996-2003: the History of BART expansion timeline lists the Yellow and Red lines for Colma; the Red Line article says the Red Line 'continued to terminate at Daly City' in 2003. Yellow is drawn to Colma, Red to Daly City. (3) Red Line 2005-2007: the BART chronology (Sept 22, 2005) says it terminated at Colma; the Red Line article records nothing south of Daly City. Drawn to Colma. (4) Dublin/Pleasanton 1997-2002 terminal is inferred as Daly City. (5) The Concord line's 1973 terminal is MacArthur per Wikipedia; an earlier version of this layer said 12th St with no source. (6) The Feb 2004 Red Line peak extension is drawn SFO-then-Millbrae; the order is not stated. (7) Date conflicts inside Wikipedia: Yellow cut to SFO Feb 10 vs Feb 11, 2020; Red all-days service Feb 14 vs Feb 20, 2022. Neither changes a drawn year.
metadata.bart_audit: 2026-10-10: rebuilt from 12 features to 36. The old layer drew every era on the 2026 routes (e.g. Antioch - Millbrae in 1973, Richmond - Berryessa in 1972), duplicated each route once per GTFS direction, started Richmond - Daly City in 1974 (it began April 1976), dated Concord - Daly City through service to Jun 16, 1974 (the tube opened Sept 16), omitted the 1973-74 Montgomery - Daly City line, the 1995-97 Concord - South Hayward special, both SFO - Millbrae shuttles, the 2017 Warm Springs stage and every SFO/Millbrae service change of 2003-2023, and had overlapping years at each era boundary.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
